work_unit: One transcript to all 27 binary attribute decisions
timing_method: Effective wall-clock time per transcript: observed end-to-end elapsed seconds divided by 150. Model loading is excluded. No concurrency was used for JEV. Local encoder runs used the recorded CPU batching configuration.

modernbert_zero_shot.execution: 4,050 transcript-attribute NLI pairs, CPU, batch size 64; thresholds do not change inference time

modernbert_trained.execution: One frozen-encoder pass per transcript plus 27 logistic heads, CPU, transcript batch size 4

jev_choice.execution: One sequential hosted request per transcript containing 27 shared-state Choice questions; network and parsing included

jev_noul.execution: One sequential hosted request per transcript containing 27 shared-state Noul questions; network and parsing included

caveats: These values normalize every system to the same output unit, but they are effective throughput-derived times, not per-request percentile latency measurements.

ModernBERT ran locally on CPU while JEV ran on hosted TypeSafe infrastructure and includes network time, so this is a measured deployment-path comparison rather than a hardware-normalized architecture benchmark.
Threshold calibration changes quality but adds negligible inference work; variants sharing a path therefore have the same latency value.
A production comparison should additionally report warm batch-1 p50/p95, concurrency, hardware, transcript-token distribution, and cold-start behavior.
